---
title: "Organizations"
subtitle: "Names appearing in public source descriptions — not organizational histories"
---

This section will hold one page per organization once a cited public source supports more than a name. This bootstrap does **not** write organizational histories.

The names below appear in the commissioning issue’s wanted-source descriptions. Listing them here only means the archive should be able to attach evidence to those names later. It is not a claim about legal status, continuity, or a role in CSIL.

| Name as given in the commissioning issue | Why the name appears here |
| --- | --- |
| BC Rehabilitation Society (also “BC Rehab”) | Named as creator of *Keys on Freedom* and, with Greater Vancouver Home Support Society, of ECPM manual(s) |
| Greater Vancouver Home Support Society | Named with BC Rehab on ECPM manual(s) |
| Ryan & Wiggins | Named with Patricia Ryan on the Creekview 202 evaluation |
| British Columbia Ministry of Health, Continuing Care Division / Community Support Branch | Named as the likely administrative home of 1993–95 CSIL pilot/design records |
| British Columbia Ministry of Health Services | Named with James Murtagh Consulting on the November 2008 synthesis report |
| James Murtagh Consulting | Named as creator of the November 2008 synthesis report |

Names now also appear in inspected public sources (for example BC Rehab and Greater Vancouver Home Support Society in the [Roeher bibliography](../sources/1990s-roeher-if-bibliography.qmd); Ministry of Health on the [2008 review citation](../sources/wanted-2008-program-review.qmd)). Listing a name is still not an organizational history.

Creekview is treated on this site as a [history placeholder](../history/creekview.qmd), not as an organization record, because inspected sources describe a co-op apartment / project, not a corporate form.

When you add an organization page, separate documented functions (cited) from later attributions, and link every claim to a [source record](../sources/index.qmd).
